lines.trans: Nastya, please stop torturing me.
And why are you angry with me?
You and I argued over a trifle.
For me this question was important.
You yourself wanted to argue a bit yesterday.
But I did not want such a foolish offense.
Forgive me if I hurt you badly.
Do you really regret your words?
I very sincerely ask your forgiveness.
It is also very hard for me to stay angry long.
Let us forget this argument right now.
Good, I agree to make peace with you.
You are the kindest and most beautiful girl.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: It's an important question.
I have important business.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.trans: I have a question.
It's a very important matter.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'yesterday'.

examples.trans: Yesterday I was at home.
Yesterday was Friday.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid?
That was a silly joke.

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.trans: Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'girl'.

examples.text: Девушки, как я, у тебя не будет!
examples.trans: You'll never have a girl like me!
This is my girlfriend Lyolya.
She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.
Quiet, stop! It really hurts!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.trans: Good evening!
She is very kind.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He talks for a long time.
I waited a long time.
We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.trans: Come if you want.
And if not?
Take her if you want.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

злиться.gloss: to be angry, to get mad

meanings.en: to be angry, to get mad
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be angry', forming an aspectual pair with 'разозлиться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?
examples.trans: And do you know why you are so angry?
Don't be angry with me, please.

examples.text: Хорошо. А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?
examples.trans: Fine. Do you know why you're so angry?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'because of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('from behind') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to excuse, to forgive') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Sorry, please.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кренне').

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я вам искренне сочувствую.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I sincerely sympathize with you.
I sincerely thank you.

examples.text: Я вам искренне сочувствую, но мне пора работать.
examples.trans: I sincerely feel for you, but it is time for me to work.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: Look how beautiful you've become!
They have a very beautiful house.
She is very pretty.

meanings.note: also colloquial imperative мучай / мучь

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
Go on then, torture me, Samson!

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'offense', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I will not forget this insult.
She was left with bitter resentment.

examples.text: Я всё равно не забуду эту обиду.
examples.trans: I will not forget this insult anyway.

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offend, to hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
He didn't want to offend anyone.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть. А ты что здесь делаешь?
examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you. And what are you doing here?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: перестань(те)! = stop it!, oh come on!

examples.text: Да перестаньте! Я двадцать лет в карты не играла.
examples.trans: Oh, stop it! I haven't played cards for twenty years.
The rain finally stopped.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('here you are') (handing something over) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: A coffee, please.
Thank you! — You're welcome.
Please see him out.

meanings.en: to make up, to make peace
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мириться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to make up', forming an aspectual pair with 'мириться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Когда-нибудь ты захочешь помириться со своим папой.
examples.trans: Someday you will want to make up with your dad.

examples.text: Я сто раз хотела с ним помириться!
examples.trans: I wanted to make up with him a hundred times!

examples.text: Хорошо, я согласна помириться с тобой.
examples.trans: Good, I agree to make peace with you.

поспорить.gloss: to make a bet, wager, argue

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'спорить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to make a bet', forming an aspectual pair with 'спорить'.

examples.trans: Let's make a bet, chef.
Let's make a bet, chef!

examples.text: Я поспорил, что он сбежит сам.
examples.trans: I bet that he will run away on his own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?
Why are you here?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Secondary conversational sense ('to beg') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He's asking for help.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness, apologise

examples.trans: I apologise.
He is asking me to forgive him.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'trifle, trivial matter' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is a trifle more important than your son's health?
It is a mere trifle.

examples.text: Мы с тобой поспорили из-за пустяка.
examples.trans: You and I argued over a trifle.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: I'll do it myself.
He knows himself.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.en: to be angry, to be cross
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ердиться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be angry', forming an aspectual pair with 'рассердиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Just don't be angry.
Are you angry?

examples.text: Нин, только не сердись, ладно? Он всё помоет.
examples.trans: Nina, just don't be angry, okay? He'll wash everything.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: I loved him so much!
The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.trans: But you gave your word!
He keeps his word.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

examples.trans: I agree.

examples.text: Я полностью согласен с вашим предложением по новому меню!
examples.trans: I completely agree with your proposal for the new menu!

examples.text: Все повара были согласны остаться вечером и помочь шефу.
examples.trans: All the cooks agreed to stay in the evening and help the chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожалеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to regret, be sorry', paired with 'посожалеть'.

examples.text: Я очень сожалею о своих словах.
examples.trans: I deeply regret my words.

examples.text: Я сильно ошиблась и очень сожалею об этом.
examples.trans: I was very mistaken and deeply regret it.

examples.text: Ты действительно сожалеешь о своих словах?
examples.trans: Do you really regret your words?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bet, wager, dispute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a bet, wager, dispute.
I agree to this bet!
I will definitely win this bet.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What is this?
He's so kind.
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + dative: мне тяжело = it's hard for me
Secondary conversational sense ('heavily') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: It's hard for me.
It's hard for you right now.

examples.text: Аркаша, я понимаю, тебе сейчас тяжело. Но…
examples.trans: Arkasha, I understand, it's hard for you right now. But...

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
Good! Everything's fine over there.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
